Hi Rachel — thanks, schedule looks great. One small hiccup: when Rachel's invite arrived in my inbox the event shows as "2:00 PM" on my calendar even though the invite subject says 9:00 AM. I think the ICS may have been created without a TZ anchor and Google is interpreting it relative to the organizer's calendar. A few notes that may help: 

- I work on a laptop set to America/New_York. I briefly traveled to London last month and my calendar default temporarily flip-flopped; I reset it, but forwarded/anchored ICSes sometimes still float.
- Could you confirm which timezone the invite is anchored to (America/New_York / Europe/London / UTC)?
- If possible, please re-send the invite with the timezone explicitly set and include the UTC timestamp (Google's UI will then show correct local times for everyone).

We also have teammates in APAC (Ben) and EMEA (Karthik) who will likely join — happy to propose a couple of alternate slots that cover US/EU/APAC windows if the 9:00 AM ET slot creates trouble for them.

For context: when an ICS lacks TZ definitions Google sometimes treats the time as "floating" and displays it in the recipient's calendar zone without conversion, which leads to a local-time mismatch.

Thanks — I'll loop Ben/Karthik to propose options and we can rebook.

Cheers,
Grace O'Connor
Director, West Coast Sales
Redwood Inference
